What's Happening?

SpaceX will be completely reusing an autonomously recovered booster. This has never been done before. Comparisons to Space Shuttle at the bottom. They will be relaunching the 15 story first stage booster that was their first recovered at sea on April 2016. This is exactly what the former kings of aerospace, Boeing and Lockheed, were saying was literally impossible and later changed to economically infeasible.

Should this flight succeed it will mark a dramatic shift in spaceflight. As the analogy often goes if 747s were thrown away after each flight, like rockets are today, you'd be paying about a million dollars for a ticket. Instead, since they're reused you can get tickets for $50. On the contrary should it fail, it will be a major obstacle for SpaceX to recover from. Whether or not its related to the reuse, reuse will be blamed in the public eye and it will severely hamstring the entire business model before it even gets started. There's pressure and then there's this.

So...?

SpaceX's ultimate goal is to get humans and cargo transiting regularly from Earth to Mars and eventually to begin a human colony on Mars effectively turning humans into a multi planetary species. To facilitate this SpaceX has designed a ship that is monumentally larger than anything ever built. But it will also be comparably more expensive. These sort of rockets, which we can really begin to start calling space ships, are impossible to develop when their use still entails just throwing away their rockets. This method of disposal also means any rocket trips are going to be one-way affairs. Rocket reuse is a key step here. Incidentally it would of course also enable radically cheaper flights for things like local space tourism, space research, and of course commercial space endeavors.

Should be fun!

Space Shuttle?

The Space Shuttle program had some limited reusability on paper, but it was very limited in reality. The most visible recovered components -the giant iconic tubes on the ship- were solid rocket boosters. Solid rocket boosters, as compared to liquid fuel engines, are basically giant firecrackers. Once ignited and unstoppable destructive explosion is triggered that's used to generate thrust. The main benefit is that they're cheap. The reuse here came down to launching the ship, discarding the used tubes into the ocean and then later fishing them out after a saltwater bath. Suffice to say there wasn't much value there. The space shuttle main engines did offer limited reuse after extensive refurbishing.

Uzboi Vallis is a long valley on Mars (More info in comments)

Uzboi Vallis is a long valley on Mars that scientists believe was once filled with running water before being temporarily dammed by the rim of a freshly formed crater. It was subsequently drained when water levels rose over the top of the dam, creating a breach. Layers of sediment deposits seen in alcoves throughout the valley and its tributaries contain a type of clay that is different from clays found in the rest of the valley, data from NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter reveals. Erosion from the lake's surroundings may have dumped this sediment here as the water drained out. — Hanneke Weitering
